claims.claim: mean allochthony in 18 Québec lakes was 0.31 in cladocerans, 0.18 in cyclopoids and 0.16 in calanoids (Berggren et al. 2014; abstract only)
claims.source_value: the abstract: Cladocera had 'the highest mean allochthony (0.31; compared to 0.18 in Cyclopoida and 0.16 in Calanoida)', 18 lakes in Quebec
claims.note: full text not read. Per the abstract, allochthony is the share of body carbon from terrestrial sources, from a δ2H + δ13C three-source mixing model (terrestrial, phytoplanktonic, benthic) across lakes spanning DOM and trophic gradients; the routes differ (calanoids' allochthony linked to detrital food chains based on particulate organic matter, cyclopoids' to DOM-based ones, cladocerans' to both; the abstract stresses the microbial food web's role). The digits match the abstract; whether 0.31 is a mean of lake means and its spread need the paper

claims.claim: cladoceran allochthony 0.31 (Berggren et al. 2014), supporting bacteria in the small cladocerans' food
claims.note: as above; note that allochthony is terrestrial carbon by any route (detrital particles as well as bacteria), so it is not a direct measure of a bacterial diet share
